name: SIA Project 25 26
description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin (which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its file path on the server). The possible problem categories are:
• Waterworks – Drinking water
• Architectural Barriers
• Sewerage
• Public Lighting
• Waste
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights
• Roads and Urban Furniture
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds
• Other
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section). If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), two cases are possible:
- Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer can mark the report as resolved. Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company (bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if previously configured by the municipal administrator.
- Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state.

C. CITIZEN UPDATES
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description. Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the same rules as for their own reports).

D. STATISTICS
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

highLevelGoals: Allow citizens to report urban issues such as potholes, broken streetlights, or garbage, fostering civic engagement and improving public services through direct feedback.
Ensure citizens can view reports on an interactive map and summary table, with filtering and sorting options, to increase transparency and awareness of urban issues.
Enable citizens to receive notifications and messages regarding their reports, and allow staff to communicate updates and comments, building trust and accountability.
Enable anonymous users to view public statistics and the interactive map of reports to promote public awareness and encourage civic involvement without requiring registration.
Enable the Organization Office to review, approve, or reject citizen reports with mandatory explanations for rejections, ensuring accountability and quality control.
Allow Technical Office Staff to assign reports to appropriate departments or external companies based on category, ensuring timely and accurate resolution of urban issues.
Offer public statistics on report trends and categories, and private analytics for administrators to monitor system performance and resource allocation.
Ensure the system is released as open-source software and made available through https://developers.italia.it/ to promote interoperability and scalability across Italian public administrations.
lowLevelGoals: Citizen submits a report with location, description, category, and optional photos or attachments.
Citizen views the current status of their submitted report and receives notifications about updates.

Citizen applies filters and sorting options to view reports based on specific criteria.
Non-registered user views public statistics on report trends and categories without logging in.
Non-registered user views the public interactive map of reports without authentication.
Organization Office Staff reviews a citizen report and decides to approve or reject it with mandatory explanation for rejection.
Technical Office Staff assigns a report to a department or external company based on its category.
Municipal Administrator views public statistics on report trends and categories.
Municipal Administrator accesses private analytics to monitor system performance and resource allocation.

Municipal Administrator publishes the system as open-source software on https://developers.italia.it/.

baselineCritiques.actors: The actors list is mostly representative of the system's description, but it lacks clarity in distinguishing between roles that might overlap or could be more precisely defined. Specifically, "Organization Office Staff" and "Technical Office Staff" are not clearly differentiated in their responsibilities based on the provided description. Additionally, while "Municipal Administrator" is mentioned, its specific tasks (e.g., configuring system settings) are not explicitly aligned with typical administrative roles in such systems. The omission of a role for managing notifications or handling public statistics access could also be considered.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are well-defined and align with the software description, covering all key functionalities such as citizen participation, reporting, communication, public access, administrative tasks, and open-source availability. No contradictions or omissions were detected.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-aligned with the high-level goals and actors, covering all necessary functional aspects of the Participium system. There are no contradictions or omissions, and each goal corresponds to a specific action an actor can perform. The system's description is fully represented in both high-level and low-level goals.

hlg_c7b4355f5aaf04ca_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable citizens to submit, track, and interact with urban issue reports while receiving real-time notifications and public visibility of report status and location, including direct messaging with municipal operators and following other users’ reports.
hlg_c7b4355f5aaf04ca_001.rationale: llg_001 enables citizens to initiate reports with metadata and media; llg_002 provides state-change notifications via configurable channels; llg_003 allows direct messaging with operators and chatbots; llg_004 offers public visualization of reports via map and table with personal report visibility; llg_005 enables following other reports and receiving updates for those followed — together, these form a complete citizen-facing urban reporting and engagement system with notification, interaction, and public visibility capabilities.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Submit a new urban issue report
Receive automated notifications for report state changes
Receive direct messages from municipal operators
View public report map and summary table
Follow other citizens’ reports and receive updates

hlg_b9167a622cc75e91_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide citizens with dual-view access to public reports — an interactive map view with geolocation markers and a summary table with metadata — both supporting dynamic filtering and sorting by category, status, or date, with the capability to display reports based on citizen-selected location.
hlg_b9167a622cc75e91_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to display public reports on an interactive map with geolocation; llg_002 adds the capability to display reports in a summary table with metadata; llg_003 adds the capability to apply dynamic filters by category, status, or date to either view; llg_004 adds the capability to sort reports by category, status, or date in either view. All four capabilities are distinct and must be preserved, including the dual-view presentation and location-based display.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Display public reports on interactive map with geolocation
Display public reports in summary table with metadata
Apply filters to reports by category, status, or date
Sort reports by category, status, or date

hlg_853e84d06ed9fe58_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Citizen receives multi-channel notifications and direct interactions regarding their own and others' submitted reports, including real-time platform alerts, email updates, direct messages from staff, chatbot interactions, and follow-based notifications for other reports.
hlg_853e84d06ed9fe58_001.rationale: llg_001 enables citizens to view their report status and updates; llg_002 adds real-time platform notifications for state changes; llg_003 adds email notifications with user-configurable opt-out; llg_004 enables direct messaging with municipal staff via the platform; llg_005 introduces chatbot interaction for report-related updates; llg_006 adds the capability to follow other citizens' reports and receive notifications for those updates — which is unrelated to the citizen’s own report and introduces a social/observational layer not present in the other goals.
source_low_level_goal_ids: View submitted report status and updates
Receive platform notifications for report state changes
Receive email notifications for report state changes
Receive direct messages from municipal staff via platform
Interact with chatbot for report updates
Follow other citizens' reports and receive notifications

hlg_ccc7734d1de6e0ef_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide public, anonymous access to aggregated report statistics and an interactive map of report locations without requiring user authentication.
hlg_ccc7734d1de6e0ef_001.rationale: llg_001 enables non-registered users to view public statistics on report trends and categories, which implies data aggregation and visualization for public consumption. llg_002 enables non-registered users to view a public interactive map of reports, which implies spatial visualization and location-based data presentation. Together, these LLGs define a scope of public-facing, anonymous data visualization tools focused on report trends and geographic distribution — no authentication is required for either capability.
source_low_level_goal_ids: View public statistics on report trends
View public interactive map without login

hlg_fc8aaf6fc932edfc_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable citizen report review and decision-making with mandatory justification for rejection by organization office staff.
hlg_fc8aaf6fc932edfc_001.rationale: llg_001 introduces the capability for organization office staff to review citizen reports and make binary decisions (approve or reject) with mandatory explanation required for rejection. No other LLGs are provided, so the reconstructed goal captures only this single functional capability without adding or omitting anything.

parsed_response.rationale:
The current set of high-level goals (HLGs) comprehensively covers all independent functional outcomes required for the identified actors. Each actor's documented responsibilities are reflected in at least one HLG, and no independently missing outcome was found.

1. Citizen: The HLGs 'Enable Citizen Participation in Urban Management', 'Provide Transparent and Accessible Reporting System', and 'Support Real-Time Communication Between Citizens and Municipal Staff' cover reporting, map interaction, and communication features.
2. Non-Registered User: The HLG 'Allow Non-Registered Users to Access Public Information' addresses the ability to view public statistics and the interactive map without logging in.
3. Organization Office Staff: The HLG 'Ensure Efficient Review and Approval of Citizen Reports' encompasses report review, approval, or rejection responsibilities.
4. Technical Office Staff: The HLG 'Facilitate Report Assignment and Management Based on Category' covers assigning reports to appropriate departments or external companies based on category.
5. Municipal Administrator: The HLGs 'Provide Public and Private Statistical Insights' and 'Make Participium Open-Source and Available to All Italian Public Administrations' address statistical insights and system availability, respectively.

No independently missing high-level outcomes were identified in the provided software description or current set of HLGs.

The source describes a specific capability for external maintenance companies to interact with the system (Case 1), including moving reports to 'In Progress' and exchanging comments with the technical office. While 'Technical Office Staff' have a goal for assignment and management, there is no HLG representing the 'External Maintenance Personnel' (or the 'External Company' entity) who perform the actual work and communicate with the office. The current HLGs cover the internal municipal workflow but miss the external service provider's interaction capability.

5. Facilitating communication between citizens and external maintenance companies through the system.
6. Providing public and private statistics on reported issues.

goals.name: Enable Citizen Participation in Urban Management
goals.description: Allow citizens to report urban issues such as potholes, broken streetlights, or garbage, fostering civic engagement and improving public services through direct feedback.

actor.name: Citizen
actor.description: Registered user who submits reports, receives updates, and can follow other reports.

goals.description: Ensure citizens can view reports on an interactive map and summary table, with filtering and sorting options, to increase transparency and awareness of urban issues.

goals.description: Enable the Organization Office to review, approve, or reject citizen reports with mandatory explanations for rejections, ensuring accountability and quality control.

hlg_c7b4355f5aaf04ca_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable citizens to submit, track, and interact with urban issue reports while receiving real-time notifications and public visibility of report status and location, including direct messaging with municipal operators and following other users’ reports.
hlg_c7b4355f5aaf04ca_001.rationale: llg_001 enables citizens to initiate reports with metadata and media; llg_002 provides state-change notifications via configurable channels; llg_003 allows direct messaging with operators and chatbots; llg_004 offers public visualization of reports via map and table with personal report visibility; llg_005 enables following other reports and receiving updates for those followed — together, these form a complete citizen-facing urban reporting and engagement system with notification, interaction, and public visibility capabilities.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Submit a new urban issue report
Receive automated notifications for report state changes
Receive direct messages from municipal operators
View public report map and summary table
Follow other citizens’ reports and receive updates

hlg_b9167a622cc75e91_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide citizens with dual-view access to public reports — an interactive map view with geolocation markers and a summary table with metadata — both supporting dynamic filtering and sorting by category, status, or date, with the capability to display reports based on citizen-selected location.
hlg_b9167a622cc75e91_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to display public reports on an interactive map with geolocation; llg_002 adds the capability to display reports in a summary table with metadata; llg_003 adds the capability to apply dynamic filters by category, status, or date to either view; llg_004 adds the capability to sort reports by category, status, or date in either view. All four capabilities are distinct and must be preserved, including the dual-view presentation and location-based display.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Display public reports on interactive map with geolocation
Display public reports in summary table with metadata
Apply filters to reports by category, status, or date
Sort reports by category, status, or date

hlg_853e84d06ed9fe58_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Citizen receives multi-channel notifications and direct interactions regarding their own and others' submitted reports, including real-time platform alerts, email updates, direct messages from staff, chatbot interactions, and follow-based notifications for other reports.
hlg_853e84d06ed9fe58_001.rationale: llg_001 enables citizens to view their report status and updates; llg_002 adds real-time platform notifications for state changes; llg_003 adds email notifications with user-configurable opt-out; llg_004 enables direct messaging with municipal staff via the platform; llg_005 introduces chatbot interaction for report-related updates; llg_006 adds the capability to follow other citizens' reports and receive notifications for those updates — which is unrelated to the citizen’s own report and introduces a social/observational layer not present in the other goals.
source_low_level_goal_ids: View submitted report status and updates
Receive platform notifications for report state changes
Receive email notifications for report state changes
Receive direct messages from municipal staff via platform
Interact with chatbot for report updates
Follow other citizens' reports and receive notifications

hlg_ccc7734d1de6e0ef_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide public, anonymous access to aggregated report statistics and an interactive map of report locations without requiring user authentication.
hlg_ccc7734d1de6e0ef_001.rationale: llg_001 enables non-registered users to view public statistics on report trends and categories, which implies data aggregation and visualization for public consumption. llg_002 enables non-registered users to view a public interactive map of reports, which implies spatial visualization and location-based data presentation. Together, these LLGs define a scope of public-facing, anonymous data visualization tools focused on report trends and geographic distribution — no authentication is required for either capability.
source_low_level_goal_ids: View public statistics on report trends
View public interactive map without login

hlg_fc8aaf6fc932edfc_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a citizen report workflow that enables Organization Office Staff to review reports for approval or rejection with mandatory rejection explanations, automatically assign approved reports to technical offices based on category, track and update report state transitions throughout the lifecycle, and persist rejection explanations for auditability.
hlg_fc8aaf6fc932edfc_001.rationale: llg_001 enables human review and decision-making with mandatory rejection justification; llg_002 introduces automated assignment to technical offices based on category and state transition to 'In Progress'; llg_003 manages the full lifecycle state transitions including 'Work in Progress' and 'Suspended'; llg_004 ensures mandatory rejection explanations are logged for accountability — together, these define a complete workflow with human review, automated routing, state tracking, and audit logging, with no omitted or generalized functionality.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Review citizen report for approval or rejection
Assign approved report to technical office based on category
Track review status and update report state
Log mandatory rejection explanation for rejected reports

hlg_ff4642dfb9b0a7fb_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the lifecycle of technical reports by assigning them to responsible parties, tracking their status through defined phases (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected, Resolved), and handling manual updates for external entities without system access.
hlg_ff4642dfb9b0a7fb_001.rationale: llg_001 enables assignment of reports to departments or external companies based on category. llg_002 updates status to 'In Progress' post-assignment. llg_003 updates status to 'Work in Progress' upon intervention start. llg_004 updates status to 'Suspended' for organizational or technical reasons. llg_005 updates status to 'Rejected' with mandatory explanation. llg_006 updates status to 'Resolved' after external company or internal completion. llg_007 provides manual status update for external companies without system access — this introduces an outlier capability that must be explicitly included to expose the mismatch between automated and manual handling.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Assign report to appropriate department or external company
Update report status to In Progress after assignment
Update report status to Work in Progress after intervention start
Update report status to Suspended for organizational or technical reasons
Update report status to Rejected with mandatory explanation
Update report status to Resolved after external company completion
Manually update report status for external companies without system access

hlg_ff99f6f5d954d8db_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Municipal Administrator to view both public report statistics and private system performance analytics for comprehensive oversight of report trends and infrastructure health.
hlg_ff99f6f5d954d8db_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the Municipal Administrator to view public report statistics and trends, which supports transparency and trend analysis for public-facing data. llg_002 enables access to private system performance analytics, which supports internal monitoring of system health and resource allocation. Together, these capabilities form a dual-view oversight system: one for public data trends and one for private system metrics — no other capability is inferred or omitted, and the reconstructed goal explicitly includes both distinct domains to preserve the full scope.
source_low_level_goal_ids: View public report statistics and trends
View private system performance analytics

hlg_bf787da4fb4e0b50_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Prepare and publish a municipal system as open-source software on https://developers.italia.it/, including configuring system settings for release and executing the public publication.
hlg_bf787da4fb4e0b50_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to configure system settings specifically for open-source release and integration with https://developers.italia.it/. llg_002 adds the capability to publish the system as open-source on that platform. Together, they form a complete scope covering both configuration and publication, with no hidden or inferred functionality.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Configure system settings for open-source release
Publish system as open-source on developers.italia.it

hlg_73541f749496e285_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement an automated report assignment system that configures, validates, triggers, and logs rules for assigning specific report categories to external maintenance companies without manual intervention, while ensuring access compliance and auditability.
hlg_73541f749496e285_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to configure automatic assignment rules linking report categories to external companies; llg_002 adds the capability to validate that external companies have access to Participium before rules can be applied; llg_003 adds the capability to trigger automatic assignment upon report submission matching configured categories; llg_004 adds the capability to log each rule’s configuration for audit and administrative review. All four capabilities are distinct and must be preserved as they collectively define the system’s scope.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Configure Automatic Assignment Rule for Report Category
Validate External Company Access for Automatic Assignment
Trigger Automatic Assignment on Report Submission
Log Automatic Assignment Rule Configuration

The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the parent high-level goal (HLG) 'Ensure Efficient Review and Approval of Citizen Reports'. Each LLG is directly supported by the source description, accurately representing essential aspects such as report review, assignment to technical offices, state tracking, and mandatory rejection explanations. No essential capability is missing or misrepresented.

LLG_001: 'Review citizen report for approval or rejection' - This aligns with the Organization Office Staff's responsibility to evaluate reports (source: 'Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review').

LLG_002: 'Assign approved report to technical office based on category' - This corresponds to the system's automatic assignment of reports to relevant technical offices post-approval (source: 'After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category').

LLG_003: 'Track review status and update report state' - This encapsulates the various states a report can transition through (source: 'The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected') and the system's role in updating these states.

LLG_004: 'Log mandatory rejection explanation for rejected reports' - This mirrors the requirement for written explanations upon rejection (source: 'If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company, two cases are possible... In case of rejection, a written explanation from the Organization Office is mandatory').

While all LLGs are supported and non-redundant, there's room for improvement in clarity and conciseness. For instance, 'Track review status and update report state' could be more precisely described as 'Update Report State Based on Review Decisions'.

The children correctly decompose the parent goal based on the source description. llg_001 covers the manual review and decision process. llg_002 captures the automatic assignment and state transition to 'In Progress' described in Section B. llg_003 covers the lifecycle state tracking (Pending, In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected). llg_004 ensures the mandatory written explanation for rejections is captured. All actions are documented, correctly scoped, and non-redundant.
Review and approval is a distinct, staff-focused outcome.

hlg_c7b4355f5aaf04ca_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable citizens to submit, track, and interact with urban issue reports while receiving real-time notifications and public visibility of report status and location, including direct messaging with municipal operators and following other users’ reports.
hlg_c7b4355f5aaf04ca_001.rationale: llg_001 enables citizens to initiate reports with metadata and media; llg_002 provides state-change notifications via configurable channels; llg_003 allows direct messaging with operators and chatbots; llg_004 offers public visualization of reports via map and table with personal report visibility; llg_005 enables following other reports and receiving updates for those followed — together, these form a complete citizen-facing urban reporting and engagement system with notification, interaction, and public visibility capabilities.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Submit a new urban issue report
Receive automated notifications for report state changes
Receive direct messages from municipal operators
View public report map and summary table
Follow other citizens’ reports and receive updates

hlg_b9167a622cc75e91_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide citizens with dual-view access to public reports — an interactive map view with geolocation markers and a summary table with metadata — both supporting dynamic filtering and sorting by category, status, or date, with the capability to display reports based on citizen-selected location.
hlg_b9167a622cc75e91_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to display public reports on an interactive map with geolocation; llg_002 adds the capability to display reports in a summary table with metadata; llg_003 adds the capability to apply dynamic filters by category, status, or date to either view; llg_004 adds the capability to sort reports by category, status, or date in either view. All four capabilities are distinct and must be preserved, including the dual-view presentation and location-based display.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Display public reports on interactive map with geolocation
Display public reports in summary table with metadata
Apply filters to reports by category, status, or date
Sort reports by category, status, or date

hlg_853e84d06ed9fe58_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Citizen receives multi-channel notifications and direct interactions regarding their own and others' submitted reports, including real-time platform alerts, email updates, direct messages from staff, chatbot interactions, and follow-based notifications for other reports.
hlg_853e84d06ed9fe58_001.rationale: llg_001 enables citizens to view their report status and updates; llg_002 adds real-time platform notifications for state changes; llg_003 adds email notifications with user-configurable opt-out; llg_004 enables direct messaging with municipal staff via the platform; llg_005 introduces chatbot interaction for report-related updates; llg_006 adds the capability to follow other citizens' reports and receive notifications for those updates — which is unrelated to the citizen’s own report and introduces a social/observational layer not present in the other goals.

hlg_ccc7734d1de6e0ef_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide public, anonymous access to aggregated report statistics and an interactive map of report locations without requiring user authentication.
hlg_ccc7734d1de6e0ef_001.rationale: llg_001 enables non-registered users to view public statistics on report trends and categories, which implies data aggregation and visualization for public consumption. llg_002 enables non-registered users to view a public interactive map of reports, which implies spatial visualization and location-based data presentation. Together, these LLGs define a scope of public-facing, anonymous data visualization tools focused on report trends and geographic distribution — no authentication is required for either capability.

hlg_fc8aaf6fc932edfc_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Implement a citizen report workflow that enables Organization Office Staff to review reports for approval or rejection with mandatory rejection explanations, automatically assign approved reports to technical offices based on category, track and update report state transitions throughout the lifecycle, and persist rejection explanations for auditability.
hlg_fc8aaf6fc932edfc_001.rationale: llg_001 enables human review and decision-making with mandatory rejection justification; llg_002 introduces automated assignment to technical offices based on category and state transition to 'In Progress'; llg_003 manages the full lifecycle state transitions including 'Work in Progress' and 'Suspended'; llg_004 ensures mandatory rejection explanations are logged for accountability — together, these define a complete workflow with human review, automated routing, state tracking, and audit logging, with no omitted or generalized functionality.

hlg_ff4642dfb9b0a7fb_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the lifecycle of technical reports by assigning them to responsible parties, tracking their status through defined phases (In Progress, Work in Progress, Suspended, Rejected, Resolved), and handling manual updates for external entities without system access.
hlg_ff4642dfb9b0a7fb_001.rationale: llg_001 enables assignment of reports to departments or external companies based on category. llg_002 updates status to 'In Progress' post-assignment. llg_003 updates status to 'Work in Progress' upon intervention start. llg_004 updates status to 'Suspended' for organizational or technical reasons. llg_005 updates status to 'Rejected' with mandatory explanation. llg_006 updates status to 'Resolved' after external company or internal completion. llg_007 provides manual status update for external companies without system access — this introduces an outlier capability that must be explicitly included to expose the mismatch between automated and manual handling.

hlg_c7b4355f5aaf04ca_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable citizens to submit, track, and interact with urban issue reports while receiving real-time notifications and public visibility of report status and location, including direct messaging with municipal operators and following other users’ reports.
hlg_c7b4355f5aaf04ca_001.rationale: llg_001 enables citizens to initiate reports with metadata and media; llg_002 provides state-change notifications via configurable channels; llg_003 allows direct messaging with operators and chatbots; llg_004 offers public visualization of reports via map and table with personal report visibility; llg_005 enables following other reports and receiving updates for those followed — together, these form a complete citizen-facing urban reporting and engagement system with notification, interaction, and public visibility capabilities.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Submit a new urban issue report
Receive automated notifications for report state changes
Receive direct messages from municipal operators
View public report map and summary table
Follow other citizens’ reports and receive updates

hlg_b9167a622cc75e91_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide citizens with dual-view access to public reports — an interactive map view with geolocation markers and a summary table with metadata — both supporting dynamic filtering and sorting by category, status, or date, with the capability to display reports based on citizen-selected location.
hlg_b9167a622cc75e91_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to display public reports on an interactive map with geolocation; llg_002 adds the capability to display reports in a summary table with metadata; llg_003 adds the capability to apply dynamic filters by category, status, or date to either view; llg_004 adds the capability to sort reports by category, status, or date in either view. All four capabilities are distinct and must be preserved, including the dual-view presentation and location-based display.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Display public reports on interactive map with geolocation
Display public reports in summary table with metadata
Apply filters to reports by category, status, or date

The current set of high-level goals appears to cover all independent functional outcomes required for the identified actors. Each actor has a corresponding goal that accurately represents their responsibilities and needs, as outlined in the project description and examples.

1. Citizen: The HLGs 'Enable Citizen Participation in Urban Management', 'Provide Transparent and Accessible Reporting System', and 'Support Real-Time Communication Between Citizens and Municipal Staff' cover reporting, map visualization, and communication aspects.
2. Non-Registered User: 'Allow Non-Registered Users to Access Public Information' addresses the ability to view public statistics and the interactive map without logging in.
3. Organization Office Staff: 'Ensure Efficient Review and Approval of Citizen Reports' covers report review and approval processes.
4. Technical Office Staff: 'Facilitate Report Assignment and Management Based on Category' addresses report assignment and management based on category.
5. Municipal Administrator: HLGs cover system configuration, access management for external companies, and statistical insights.

No independently missing outcomes were identified in the current set of high-level goals.

The source describes a scenario where external companies with access can move reports to 'In Progress', exchange comments with the technical office, and mark reports as 'Resolved'. While 'Technical Office Staff' have a goal for assignment, the actual execution of the work by external entities is a distinct operational outcome for a specific actor group not yet represented by a goal.

parsed_response.rationale:
After reviewing the provided software description and current high-level goals (HLGs), there are no independently missing functional outcomes for the documented actors. Each actor's responsibility is covered by an existing HLG, either directly or through a broader parent goal. Here's a summary of the mapping:

1. **Citizen**: Covered by 'Enable Citizen Participation in Urban Management', 'Provide Transparent and Accessible Reporting System', and 'Support Real-Time Communication Between Citizens and Municipal Staff'. These HLGs encompass report submission, viewing reports on a map/table, and receiving updates.
2. **Non-Registered User**: Covered by 'Allow Non-Registered Users to Access Public Information' which allows anonymous users to view public statistics and the interactive map of reports.
3. **Organization Office Staff**: Covered by 'Ensure Efficient Review and Approval of Citizen Reports' which includes preliminary review, approval/rejection with explanations, and state transitions (Pending Approval -> In Progress).
4. **Technical Office Staff**: Covered by 'Facilitate Report Assignment and Management Based on Category' which involves assigning reports to departments or external companies based on category.
5. **Municipal Administrator**: Covered by 'Provide Public and Private Statistical Insights', 'Make Participium Open-Source and Available to All Italian Public Administrations', and 'Enable Automatic Assignment of Reports to External Companies Based on Preconfigured Rules'.

No distinct, independently missing functional outcomes were found for any actor. The current HLGs provide a comprehensive overview of the system's capabilities from each stakeholder perspective.

The current HLGs cover reporting, communication, review, assignment, and statistics. However, they miss the specific capability for 'External Maintenance Personnel' (who are distinct from Technical Office Staff) to interact with the system. The source describes a specific workflow where these personnel can move reports to 'In Progress' and mark them as 'Resolved' when they have system access. While Technical Office Staff manage the reports, the ability for external workers to perform these specific lifecycle actions is an independent functional outcome for that group. Additionally, the ability for citizens to 'follow' other citizens' reports is mentioned in the source and actor description but is not explicitly covered by the 'Transparent and Accessible Reporting System' HLG, which focuses on viewing the map and table.
